Status: Wave 286 accepted (6.3): the Falcon property-value frame Class920

Method.evidence: Class920 is the property-value frame. It formats itself as ObjectIndex={0} PID={1} PropertyIndex={2} DataType={3} MaxSize={4}, and both PropertyDescription conversions name the rest: a() feeds the eight-argument constructor in order (objectIndex, propertyId, propertyIndex, propertyDataType, writeEnabled, maxSize, readRights, writeRights - parameter names read from the metadata) and a(PropertyDescription) writes the same fields back. The frame offsets confirm every pair: byte 0 object index, byte 1 property id, byte 2 property index, byte 3 the six-bit data type plus the write-enabled high bit, 16-bit max size at offset 4, and the read/write rights nibbles of byte 6 (the getter of the high nibble is the constructor seventh argument readRights, its setter preserves the low nibble).
Method.themes: New helper perf-now/formatter-blocks.py lists the free rows of every type whose GetFormattedData is already named, so the self-formatting family can be worked block by block; Falcon still has Class871 (11 free), Class890 (10), Class836/854/847/843/848/852/875/889/906 (7-8 each) waiting, all with the same evidence source.
